_note: Hand-curated. 'producer' = climacteric fruit with internal ethylene production; 'sensitive' = documented quality loss from exogenous ethylene; 'neutral' = neither documented (or not plant tissue).

sources.ams2023: USDA AMS National Organic Program, 'Ethylene — Handling' Technical Report (2023), lines 177-183: bananas, avocado and tomato listed as climacteric; strawberry listed as non-climacteric with 'little or no increase in internal ethylene production'. https://www.ams.usda.gov/sites/default/files/media/2023Technical_Report_Ethylene_Handling.pdf
sources.ucdavis_spinach: Suslow, T. & Cantwell, M. 'Spinach: Recommendations for Maintaining Postharvest Quality', UC Davis Postharvest Research & Extension Center: spinach is highly sensitive to exogenous ethylene; low levels cause accelerated yellowing; do not mix with apples, melons and tomatoes. https://postharvest.ucdavis.edu/node/8161

STRW-01.note: non-climacteric, very low producer; sensitivity not classified from a verified source
